q: storm knocked the power out two days ago and we have been living off the wood stove. tonight my father went out to bring logs in and i found him lying by the woodpile, he doesnt answer and i cant see him breathing
we are cut off by the flood since tuesday, the bridge is gone. my wife went quiet in her chair about ten minutes ago and now her lips are grey and i cannot wake her

snowed in at the cabin four days, no signal, generator ran dry last night. my brother in law was shovelling the roof, came in, sat down and just slid off the bench. he made a snoring noise and then nothing
we are on the boat anchored in the bay and the radio is dead. the skipper went below to look at the engine and when i looked down the hatch he was on the floor of the cabin not moving at all

after the quake the stairs are blocked and we are stuck on the third floor with the neighbours. the old lady from flat 6 was sitting with us and she has just gone slack, mouth open, no breath that i can feel
camping two days walk from the road. marta said she felt dizzy at breakfast, we kept walking, now she has dropped on the trail, lids half shut, and gives no reaction when i shout her name
power has been out since the ice storm. grandad needs his oxygen machine and we had it running off the car but it cut out in the night. this morning he is cold to touch and i cant find a pulse on him
lambing all week and no sleep. jim went to check the far shed an hour ago and never came back, i found him on the straw between the pens, blue round the mouth and his chest is not going up or down
the river came over the yard so we moved everything upstairs. carrying the last boxes my husband grabbed his chest and folded up on the landing. now he will not respond to me at all
hurricane went through last night, road is full of trees. we were clearing the drive and a big limb came down on my neighbour, he is under it and has stopped making any sound
third day with no power, we have been cooking on the camping stove indoors with the windows shut because of the cold. my daughter went to lie down with a headache and now i cant wake her up
tonight in the marina the old man off the next boat fell between the pontoon and his hull. two of us hauled him up onto the pontoon, he is not coughing, not doing anything, just lying there
earthquake about an hour ago, we are all out in the car park. a man next to us said his arm hurt, sat on the kerb, and now he has tipped over sideways and his face has gone purple

off grid homestead, nearest town is three hours. my partner was up the ladder fixing the solar panels, i heard a bang, she is on the ground on her back with her eyes open, not blinking, i dont think she is breathing

we have been walking out since the storm wrecked camp. tom has been coughing for days and falling behind. we stopped to rest, he lay down, and now we cant get him to wake, he takes a breath only now and then

no power and no phones since the wind took the lines down. my mother is 84 and was sat by the stove knitting, i brought her tea and her head was on her chest and her hands are cold, she isnt answering
been at the hunting cabin a week. this morning rick did not get up, i thought he was sleeping it off but he is still in the bunk at noon, stiff and cold and his eyes are a bit open

the levee broke in the night and we got onto the roof with the neighbours. their grandmother was fine when we climbed up but she is lying on the tiles now and nobody can get a word or a movement out of her

fishing trip, we are six miles out and the motor is flooded. dan was pulling the anchor, said he felt sick, and then went over backwards into the bottom of the boat. he is grey and i cant hear any breathing
we lost power in the heatwave and the fans stopped. my uncle has been in bed all day, he was hot and muttering this afternoon, now he is dry and burning and will not open his eyes or squeeze my hand

remote sheep station, flying doctor cant land in this dust. the cook came running, one of the shearers is face first on the shed floor, he had been complaining of a tight chest since lunch, no pulse that i can find

day three after the tornado, we are sleeping in the school gym. the man on the cot beside ours has diabetes and ran out of his insulin, tonight he was breathing fast and deep and now he is not rousing when his wife shakes him
flood water is still in the street so we stayed upstairs. my son is 4, he had a fever all night and a few minutes ago he went floppy in my arms and his eyes rolled up, he is not looking at me
we ran the generator in the garage because of the rain, door mostly shut. my husband went to refuel it twenty minutes ago. i just found him on the concrete next to it and he is not moving
kayak trip down the canyon, no way out for two days. at camp tonight josie stood up from the fire, said whoa, and went straight down on the sand. shes not answering and her arms are just floppy

the mine road washed out so nobody can come. old pete from the next claim walked over for coffee, sat on my step, and i came back out to find him keeled over against the rail with his tongue out and no breathing

blizzard, we are stuck in the truck on the pass with the engine off to save fuel. my dad stopped talking a while ago and i took it for sleep but no amount of shaking wakes him and his face is like wax
power cut means the stair lift is dead so i have been sleeping downstairs with mum. she called out in the night and when i got to her she was half off the bed, heavy, eyes shut, not a sound from her

we are wardens at a mountain hut, cloud is down and the phone mast is out. a walker came in soaked an hour ago, we put him by the stove, he stopped shivering and now he has slumped and i cant get any response

harvest, working till dark. the lad driving the grain cart didnt answer the radio so i walked over, he is hanging half out of the cab door, limp, there is sick down his shirt and i cant feel him breathing

after the earthquake we set up in the garden. my father in law has a bad heart, he was helping carry water and he sat down hard on the grass and then lay back. his eyes are fixed and he is not breathing

tide has cut us off on the rocks till morning. one of the lads slipped earlier and banged his head, he said he was fine and went to sleep. now he is snoring very loud and strange and we cant wake him whatever we do
the wind took the roof off the barn last night. my husband went in this morning to see to the animals and a beam came down. i can see his legs. he is not answering me when i call

off grid in the desert, truck wont start. my friend went looking for the track four hours ago in this heat, i found him sitting against a rock with his head down, skin hot, he doesnt react when i pour water on him

we are the only ones left in the village after the evacuation. the neighbour across the lane, mr kowalski, didnt light his fire today so i went in. he is in his armchair, cold, and i dont know if he is alive
long story short we are stuck at the trailhead hut with no service, the stove has been on all night, and this morning two of the group will not wake up and the third is vomiting and can hardly stand
storm brought a line down across our track. my brother stopped the quad to drag a branch clear and the next thing he was on the ground beside the wire, not moving, and the wire is still hissing
no ambulance will come out here since the bridge went. my wife has been in labour since yesterday, the baby came ten minutes ago and he is purple and limp and has not cried or taken a breath
we are in a tent camp after the floods. my baby girl is five weeks old, she fed an hour ago, and when i picked her up just now she was floppy and pale and i cant see her tummy moving
sailing overnight, i came up for my watch and the helm was empty, found my husband wedged down by the winch, clipped on but hanging in his harness, face blue, not responding

sixth day without power. the old fella next door keeps his heating on a paraffin thing. i knocked to bring him soup and saw him through the window on the kitchen floor, i got in, he is warm but i get nothing when i shake him

there is no road in winter, only the snowmobile. my husband went to cut ice for water and came back grey, said he needed to sit. he sat. now his head is back and he is making a gurgling sound and wont look at me

we were stacking sandbags all night with half the town. a woman two along from me in the line just crumpled without a word, somebody caught her, she is flat on the wet road now with her eyes rolled back
farm is cut off by snow drifts. dad went to break ice on the troughs at six. it is nine now. he is lying beside the tractor with frost on his coat and he does not move when i shake him
refuge hut, alps, storm outside, eight of us. the guide made tea, sat down against the wall and never picked it up. i touched his neck and felt nothing. somebody is saying he is only asleep

we have been on the life raft since the boat went down yesterday. the cook has not spoken since dawn and when the swell rolled him over just now he did not put a hand out. his lips are white and i cant tell if he breathes

quake dropped the ceiling in the back room. we dug my sister out, she talked to us for a minute, said she was thirsty, then her head fell to the side. she is not answering now and i think she has stopped breathing

logging camp, forty km of dirt road and the radio mast is down. a chain snapped and caught lars across the throat, he went straight over, there is not much blood but he is not moving and not breathing

the power is off so the well pump is off so i walked to the spring with grandpa. on the way back up the hill he stopped, leaned on the fence, and went down like a tree. he is face in the dirt and silent

wildfire evacuation, we are parked in a field with hundreds of cars and smoke everywhere. the lady in the van next to us is asthmatic, she was wheezing badly, now she is slumped over the wheel and has gone quiet

my wife is a type one diabetic and we have had no fridge for the insulin since the storm. she was confused at supper, went to bed, and i cannot wake her now. she is sweating and her breathing sounds wet

there has been no doctor on the island since the ferry stopped. old mrs tanaka fell in her garden this morning, we carried her in and she was talking. tonight she is not talking, one pupil is huge and she wont wake

we are holed up in the church hall after the cyclone with about forty people. a man near the door stood up fast, shouted something, and dropped. people say he was drinking. he is breathing but i cant wake him

hut book says the next party is due friday. yesterday my climbing partner got a bad headache at altitude, today he would not get out of his bag, now he is blowing pink froth and i cant get him to answer
outback, bogged to the axles, two days. my mate went quiet and red in the afternoon, i put him under the tarp. he stopped sweating and now hes floppy and wont swallow and his eyes dont follow me

snow took the phone line. my husband has been clearing the lane by hand since dawn, he came in for his dinner, said his jaw ached, and put his head down on the table. i thought he was resting. he is not breathing

earthquake, then the gas went off, then the water. we are fine but the man upstairs has not come down. i went up. his door was open and he lies by the toilet, blue in the face. no sound at all from him

remote research station, weather has grounded the plane. our mechanic was working under the snowcat, the jack slipped. we got it off him in maybe two minutes. he is not conscious and his chest looks wrong and still

the storm surge filled the ground floor. we are upstairs. my father went down in the dark to get his tablets and i heard a splash and a thud. he is lying on the stairs half in the water and wont answer

no electric for a week, we cook in the yard. my mother in law bent to stir the pot and just sat down in the dust and then lay back. her mouth is on one side and she breathes like snoring. she does not wake

caravan in the forest, off season, nobody about. my boyfriend took something for his back pain that a friend gave him, a lot i think. he is on the bed, lips blue, tiny pupils, and he breathes maybe four times a minute
we were told to shelter in place after the chemical plant fire. my son went out to bring the washing in. he came back coughing, lay on the sofa, and now i cant get him to open his eyes

bothy in the highlands, night, no reception. my friend has a nut allergy and there was something in the stew. her face swelled, she used her pen, she was wheezing, and in the last minute she went silent and floppy against the wall
since the flood we drink from the tank. everyone has had the runs but my little brother worst. he is seven. tonight he stopped answering, his eyes are sunk and he is limp like a cloth when i lift him
mustering cattle, a full day from the homestead. the horse came back without sam. we tracked back and he is on the ground in the creek bed, helmet cracked, not moving, i cant tell about his breathing

winter camp on the lake ice. my uncle was in the fishing shack with the heater on all night. this morning the door was iced shut. we forced it and he is on the floor, cherry red in the face, not waking

my husband is the lighthouse keeper and we are alone out here till the supply boat. he was painting the gallery rail, i heard him shout, and he lies at the foot of the tower steps, neck at a strange angle, not breathing

it has rained for nine days and the track is a river. my wife is 36 weeks. she had a terrible headache and swollen hands yesterday. just now she went stiff, shook all over for a minute, and now she will not wake up

mountain village, landslide closed the road. the priest was ringing the bell for the meeting and people say he just let go of the rope and sat down. he is on the stone floor now and the women are praying but nobody is doing anything
two families in one house since the storm. tonight my cousin found her husband in the outhouse, on the floor, needle beside him. he is grey, gurgling a bit, hardly any breaths. she is screaming

the wind turbine brake failed and my dad climbed up to lock it by hand. something hit him. he is hanging in his harness about four metres up, head down, arms loose, and he does not answer when we shout
ski touring, slab released above us. we dug nina out after maybe twelve minutes. there was snow packed in her mouth. she is out of the hole now, on her back, blue, and we see no breathing

trawler, north sea, force 9. the deckhand got hit by the door when the wave came, he went down hard on the steel and slid into the scuppers. hes out, there is blood from one ear, and he is breathing like a saw

farm, no power. the milking is by hand so everyone is tired. my teenage daughter fainted in the parlour this morning i thought, but that was five minutes ago and she has not come round and now her arms are jerking

we walked out of the fire zone last night, twelve km. this morning my father cant be woken. he was breathing smoke for hours before we left. his face is sooty round the nose and his breathing is a crow sound

the heating oil ran out on monday. i went to check on my aunt today. she was in bed under all the blankets, very cold, mumbling. i went to make a hot drink and when i came back she was silent and i cant find a pulse

we are doing the night watch at the flood barrier. one of the volunteers, a big man, maybe sixty, said he needed a minute and leaned on the pump. then he went. he is on his back on the gravel and somebody says he isnt breathing

narrowboat, miles from a road, canal frozen. my partner has been low for weeks. i came back from the shop walk and she is in the bunk with empty packets all round her, breathing very shallow, i cant wake her

village well, the men were cleaning it. the first one went down the rope and stopped answering. the second went after him and stopped as well. both are at the bottom now and not moving and a third wants to go

no doctor will get through the snow. my husband had the flu all week, tonight he got up for the toilet and i heard him fall. he is wedged between the bath and the wall, awake i think but his eyes are odd and now he has stopped talking

desert race support crew, sat phone is flat. a runner came into the checkpoint weaving, said he was cold, in 40 degrees, and then he just folded. he is twitching a little and wont respond and his skin is dry

it is the third night in the shelter. the woman beside us had a baby with her, maybe a few months. she just started screaming that he is cold. i looked. he is white and still and there is nothing when i touch his chest

back country hut, wood stove, six of us drying kit. the youngest, a lad of about 19, had a nosebleed and a headache all day and has now gone over sideways on the bench. he snores, he will not wake, one arm is stiff
the tractor is on its side in the ditch with the engine still running and my father is under the mudguard. i can reach his hand. it is warm. he does not grip back and i cannot hear him

after the storm we shared a cooked chicken that had been in the dead freezer. everybody is sick but my grandfather is the worst, he has been on the floor of the bathroom for an hour and now he is not answering and his lips are blue

ferry is cancelled till thursday. my neighbour is 91 and lives alone, i take her dinner. tonight she was on the hall floor in her nightdress, freezing, eyes shut. i said her name and got a sort of groan and then no more

we got the horses in before the hail. my wife was last through the gate and a stone the size of an egg hit her on the head, she dropped where she stood, in the mud, she is bleeding from the scalp and she is not moving
army surplus tent, minus fifteen, the stove pipe came off in the night. i woke with a splitting head and crawled out. my two friends are still in there in their bags and i cannot wake either of them

the path to the village is under a metre of water. my mother takes heart pills and a water pill and we ran out sunday. tonight she said the room was spinning, lost all her colour, and sank down against the wall. she is not answering me now

remote beach camp, the tide brought jellyfish in. my friend swam through them, got to the sand, said his chest was tight and he could not swallow. that was two minutes ago. he is flat out now, lips swollen, not responding

we were crossing the ford on foot after the rain, holding the rope. the current took my brother off his feet. we got him to the bank maybe three minutes later, further down. he is limp, foam round the lips, and no breathing

eight days since the quake. the aftershock tonight brought more plaster down and a woman in the next tent grabbed her chest and fell. her daughter says she has a pacemaker. i see no breathing from her

ice storm, power lines down everywhere, we have a fire going in the hearth. my husband got up to put a log on, stopped, said oh, and fell across the rug. i turned him over. his eyes are open and he is not there

on the allotment, miles from anyone, no phone on me. the old chap two plots down was digging and i saw his spade fall and then him. i ran over. he is face down in the bean row and when i roll him he is purple

crewing a yacht delivery, mid atlantic. the owner has been seasick five days and drinking nothing. tonight he would not wake for his watch. he is breathing fast and shallow, his skin stays pinched up, and he doesnt react to pain

my son and his friends were jumping off the quarry edge into the snow drifts. one of them, a boy called ivan, landed on something hard under the snow. he is lying in the drift, not crying, not moving, his lips are going blue

hill farm, power off, phones off. my husband went to free a ewe from the fence in the storm. the dog came back alone. i found him by the wall, soaked through, not shivering, stiff, and i cant tell if there is a heartbeat

the road crew cant reach us for days. grandma has been on the commode chair all morning because she felt weak, i went to help her up and she slid through my arms onto the floor. she is heavy and silent and her colour is awful

we are at a festival in the hills and the storm has shut the only road. a girl in the tent next to ours took pills from someone, she was dancing an hour ago, now she is burning hot, rigid, jaw clenched, and she wont answer anyone

our community runs on a micro hydro and it failed, so the clinic fridge and everything is off. the nurse herself collapsed in the store room while counting stock. we found her on the floor behind the door. no breathing. no pulse

storm drain behind the houses overflowed. the neighbour's teenage boy went to clear the grate and did not come back in. his mother found him lying beside it in the rain. he is cold, not shivering, not speaking, eyes closed

we were told the helicopter cant fly tonight. my climbing partner fell maybe ten metres on the last pitch and is hanging on the rope below me. i lowered him to the ledge. he is not conscious and there is a rattle when he breathes

no vehicle can get up here in the mud season. my wife was bitten on the ankle by a snake at the wood pile forty minutes ago. she was talking and scared. now her eyelids droop, she slurs, and she just stopped answering me

storm took the mast and the radio. we are drifting. my wife hit her head on the boom when it swung, she got up and said she was ok, then she lay down in the cockpit. that was an hour ago. i cant wake her and one eye looks bigger

last night of the hunting trip. my father ate, said he had heartburn, and turned in early. i heard a strange long snore from his tent and then silence. i opened it. he is on his back with his mouth open and he is not breathing

there is no light, the candles are nearly gone. my grandmother has been dying for a week, the nurse said it would come. but just now my grandfather, who was sitting with her, fell out of his chair and he is the one not breathing

dust storm, we pulled the convoy over. when it cleared the driver of the last truck was not in his cab. he was on the sand by the rear wheel, mouth and nose full of dust, limp. we cleared his mouth. still nothing from him
